findings: Stage 12 must replace the nc-01-page04-next-scene control demonstration that replays SHOW_PAGE_05 immediately before scoring which scene follows page 04. That demonstration exposes the exact correct Emma-scene target, so the scored response can be driven by the demonstrated target/cadence instead of retention of the accepted page-04-to-page-05 transition; freeze demonstrations whose scenes do not expose either side of the scored boundary, while preserving null spoken instruction, inspectable full-scene options, and counterbalanced option order.

Stage 13 must make TRAIN_MORE terminally executable. After fewer than 3 of 4 base answers, phase success requires 2 consecutive released reserve answers, but the second reserve is released only if the gate-specific problem persists; one correct first reserve can therefore leave the phase neither successful nor failed and can prevent FINISH. Define the second release and terminal transition mechanically for every first-reserve outcome without adding live material.

Stage 13 must freeze an exact PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch table from each failed gate to one presentation ID and one specific unmarked cold-retest exercise ID. The current seven-ID pool includes greeting and general self-identification blocks, while the release and return rules refer only to 'that gate'; runtime selection is therefore undefined and could become live improvisation.

Stage 13 must define teacher-turn accounting for every comprehension demonstration and SHOW_CORRECT_OPTION action, then recompute base_teacher_turn_count and the REPLAY_LESSON remaining-budget operand from that definition. The declared count of 82 accounts for modeled presentation/story turns and scored prompts but does not state whether the four mandatory control demonstrations and their feedback actions consume the 220-turn global budget, so the replay predicate is not mechanically evaluable against the actual required execution.
